chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs56007086 itself
predictions: rs56007086 shows no reproducible allele-specific TF binding in a direct assay, even though FOXA1 may occupy the broader region in MCF7.
Editing rs56007086 alone does not change TOX3 expression or breast-cancer-relevant enhancer activity.

The 16q12 breast cancer signal at this locus is better explained by a linked causal variant such as rs4784227, or by no functional effect of rs56007086; the variant has no GWAS Catalog, Open Targets, GTEx breast eQTL, or variant-specific literature support.
falsified_if: A direct allele-specific binding assay shows a reproducible TF preference for one rs56007086 allele.
CRISPR editing of rs56007086 alone changes TOX3 expression or a breast cancer phenotype in a relevant cell type.
Fine-mapping or functional dissection shows rs56007086 is the functional variant independent of other TOX3-locus variants.

chains.title: Alt allele strengthens FOXA1 binding at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies the rs56007086 region in MCF7: an ENCODE FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak in MCF-7 contains chr16:52565398:G>A. This supports FOXA1 occupancy at the locus but not allele-specific binding; the claim that the alt A allele binds FOXA1 more strongly than ref G is a hypothesis, not demonstrated by the supplied evidence. FOXA1 QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked.

The variant is annotated within the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer, and a dELS EH38E3180851 with DNase and H3K27ac signal lies 38 bp away. E03 states that no cCRE overlaps the variant and gives biosample-maximal, not MCF7-specific, signal, so the element assignment is candidate-level.
TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene, 17.6 kb upstream, and CASC16 overlaps the variant. This is proximity evidence only; there is no significant breast-tissue eQTL for this variant in GTEx v8.

MCF7 is the supplied expression context, and E07 shows a FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF-7, supporting FOXA1 occupancy at this locus in this cell type. Allele-specific occupancy in MCF7 is still untested.

TOX3 is a breast cancer candidate locus and a known TOX3 enhancer variant, rs4784227, has been linked to breast cancer. There is no variant-specific GWAS, Open Targets or literature record for rs56007086, so disease relevance is inherited from TOX3 and is indirect.

predictions: An allele-specific FOXA1 assay at rs56007086 in MCF7 shows stronger FOXA1 binding to the alt A allele than to the ref G allele.
FOXA1 depletion or CRISPRi reduces TOX3 expression or enhancer reporter activity preferentially from the alt A allele in MCF7 cells.
The FOXA1 ChIP peak at this locus is reproducible in MCF7 and maps to the rs56007086-containing sequence.
falsified_if: Allele-specific FOXA1 binding at rs56007086 shows no difference between G and A, or shows stronger binding to the ref G allele.
FOXA1 depletion does not change TOX3 expression or enhancer reporter activity in an rs56007086 genotype-dependent manner.
The FOXA1 ChIP peak does not require or map to the rs56007086 sequence, or is explained by a linked variant such as rs4784227.

chains.title: Ref allele strengthens CTCF binding near the TOX3 locus

links.claim: The claim that CTCF binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele at rs56007086 is a hypothesis. E03 reports a CTCF z-score of 1.9 for a nearby dELS 38 bp away; this is not variant-level, not allele-specific, and not MCF7-specific. CTCF QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked.

The variant is near dELS EH38E3180851 and within ENSR16_9QTBS, so altered CTCF binding could in principle affect insulator or enhancer activity. However, no cCRE overlaps the variant and the chromatin marks are biosample maxima, not MCF7-resolved.

TOX3 is 17.6 kb upstream and CASC16 overlaps the variant, so a CTCF-dependent chromatin change could affect TOX3. This is proximity only; no chromatin-conformation, eQTL or perturbation evidence ties this element to TOX3, and E08 shows no breast-tissue eQTL for the variant.
MCF7 is the supplied expression context, but the supplied evidence does not show CTCF occupancy or insulator activity at this locus in MCF7.

TOX3 is a breast cancer candidate locus and rs4784227 is a known TOX3 enhancer variant, but rs56007086 has no GWAS, Open Targets or variant-specific literature record. The disease link is therefore indirect and gene-level.

predictions: An allele-specific CTCF assay at rs56007086 shows stronger CTCF binding to the ref G allele than to the alt A allele.
CTCF depletion changes local chromatin conformation or TOX3 expression in an rs56007086 genotype-dependent manner in MCF7 cells.
The nearby CTCF signal maps to the rs56007086-containing sequence rather than only to the adjacent dELS.
falsified_if: No allele-specific CTCF binding is detected at rs56007086.
CTCF depletion does not affect chromatin conformation or TOX3 expression at this locus.
The CTCF signal maps to a different element and is not influenced by rs56007086.

The variant is annotated within ENSR16_9QTBS and lies 38 bp from dELS EH38E3180851, which carries enhancer chromatin marks. No cCRE overlaps the variant and the marks are not MCF7-specific, so this is candidate-level element evidence.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb upstream and CASC16 overlaps the variant. This is proximity only; there is no breast-tissue eQTL for rs56007086 in GTEx v8 and no contact or perturbation evidence linking this element to TOX3.

checks.why: The entire C1 chain rests on an unevidenced FOXA1 binding claim; an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in MCF7 would either ground or kill C1.binding, and the same call also tests whether any of the three guessed TFs has real occupancy here.

If rs56007086 is an eQTL for TOX3 in breast tissue, the element/gene link common to C1-C3 becomes plausible and the null loses ground; if not, the proximity-only gene step stays weak in all three chains.

E04/E05 show no association record, so the decisive question is whether any published functional study exists for this variant itself (or only for rs4784227); a variant-specific search directly tests the phenotype steps of C1-C3 and the premise of C4.
